guide.title: Bring your own account
guide.subtitle: What changes when the provider account stays yours
guide.excerpt: The platform has no provider account of its own. That one design decision changes who owns the numbers, who holds the quota, and who appears on the invoice.

p: You keep your account with Twilio, Vonage, Infobip, MessageBird, Plivo or AWS. You give the platform credentials with permission to send. When a message goes out, the platform calls that provider using your credentials, from your account, against your quota, and the provider bills you at the rate you negotiated with them.

The platform never holds a provider account, never resells message volume, and never appears on the invoice you get from your provider. What you pay the platform is a flat subscription for the orchestration layer and nothing else.

list: Your sender numbers stay yours. If you stop using the platform, the numbers, registrations and history with the provider do not move.
Your negotiated rate stays your negotiated rate. There is no markup applied on top of it, because there is no message margin to apply it to.
Your relationship with the provider stays direct. When they change a limit, run a maintenance window or need to verify your account, you deal with them as their customer, not through us.

sections.h: What it does not buy you
list: It does not transfer your provider account, approvals or credit line. Those remain yours to keep in good standing.
It does not make your quota larger. Your provider grants you a rate; the platform can only queue to it, never raise it.
It does not put us between you and your provider in a dispute. We cannot escalate on your behalf, because we are not their customer.

sections.h: Why a flat subscription is the honest shape
p: If message volume is billed by your provider and not by us, then a per-message price on our side would be a margin on somebody else’s bill, with no corresponding cost of ours. A flat subscription keyed to the things we actually operate — how many connections you run, how fast you may submit, how long logs are kept — is the shape that matches where the work is.
